title: SE Rebuttal Orchestra: Demo Practice and Objection Tuning
summary: Internal SE enablement: rapid demo runs with focused objection handling. Practiced three demo scenarios (startup latency-first, enterprise compliance-first, cost-sensitive E-com). Major outcomes: tighten 90s opener, simplify VPC explanation, finalize new two-slide battlecard on Dedicated vs Hosted. Action owners assigned for battlecard updates and 1:1 coaching slots.
action_items: Maya - update Dedicated vs Hosted battlecard and send to field by 2025-12-03
Liam - record short GIFs demonstrating KV-cache effect and share link by 2025-12-02
Priya - compile SOC2/ISO one-pager with links to compliance docs and send to team by 2025-12-05
Devon - schedule 30-min 1:1 coaching slots for new hires (Nina + 2) by 2025-12-01
next_steps: Share recording + clips of best rebuttals
Push battlecard v2 to Confluence and Slack #field-se
Book two follow-ups: demo coaching + competitive deep-dive
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-28
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 75 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (AE), Liam O'Connor (SE), Priya Shah (SE), Ethan Morales (Product), Jordan Matthews (field SE), Sofia Ruiz (sr AE), Devon Park (sales ops), Nina Patel (new hire)

-- Auto-generated summary (brief) --
We ran three roleplay demos with focused objections; captured wins and areas to tighten.

[00:00:00] Maya: ok hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um quick agenda, two warmup demos, then two shot rebuttal rounds and then we capture action items, sound good?
[00:00:12] Jordan: yep loud and clear, excited to watch the new opener
[00:00:18] Liam: just a reminder for the roleplay, Jordan will be latency-first startup, Sofia will be compliance-first enterprise, Nina you'll be cost-sensitive e-com later
[00:00:30] Maya: perfect, I'll do a 90 second elevator and then Liam will take the walkthrough
[00:00:36] Maya: hi I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, we help engineering teams ship LLM features with predictable latency and lower token costs, we run the same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so you don't have to rewrite when you scale, and teams often cut 20-to-50 percent off per-token spend with our batching and KV caching best practices, um that's the short version
[00:00:58] (brief chuckle)
[00:01:02] Jordan (roleplay): okay so I'm a startup, we care about p99 latency under 200ms, what's your smallest footprint offering and how quickly can we pilot?
[00:01:12] Liam: so great question, for latency-first workloads we recommend our hosted API with the low-latency model profile or Dedicated if you want predictable p99 at scale; for pilot quick start you can test in hours using our sandbox, we can also run a micro-benchmark with your payloads in a day or two
[00:01:28] Jordan: whats the difference between hosted and dedicated again?
[00:01:32] Priya: short answer: hosted is fastest to go live and managed, Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for throughput and isolation, you get capacity guarantees, and campaign-level latency SLOs, and there's an option for burst capacity
[00:01:45] Jordan: and data? we can't send PII outside our cloud
[00:01:48] Liam: yeah completely fair — for PII-heavy stuff we'd do Private (VPC or on-prem) or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS and strict retention policies, we also offer audit logs and SAML SSO, and we'll sign data handling appendices if needed
[00:02:02] Maya: quick note for the team: that question usually surfaces early, lead with either 'we have Private for PII' or 'we can instrument token redaction and KMS integration depending on contract' depending on buyer
[00:02:15] Jordan: ok that helps
[00:02:20] (transition)
[00:02:24] Maya: second scenario Sofia, you're enterprise compliance-first, hit me with the hardest objection
[00:02:30] Sofia (roleplay): we've got SOC2 and ISO audits coming up, plus procurement wants to know where logs live, who can access them, and do you have tamper-proof audit trails
[00:02:40] Liam: yes we publish SOC2 Type II status, we support enterprise KMS, we have immutable audit logs option and we can restrict access via RBAC and IP allowlists, if procurement wants we can provide a third-party attestation and an architecture diagram
[00:02:53] Sophia: can you show me the attestation quickly?
[00:02:56] Ethan: (screenshare note) link to compliance pack in chat: https://redwood.example.com/compliance-pack
[00:03:00] Sophia: (murmur) okay that's good
[00:03:05] Maya: team note - when procurement asks for 'attestation', don't say 'we're working on it' instead say 'here's the SOC2 report and our KMS integration guide' and offer an onsite or calendared walkthrough with security
[00:03:18] (15-second pause)
[00:03:34] Nina (roleplay): quick question — how do you maintain consistency if we switch cloud regions or do a hybrid?
[00:03:40] Priya: the platform abstracts deployment; same API, models pinned by version, and smart routing handles ephemeral fallbacks; caveat: model latency will vary by region and the runtime picks kernels by hardware, so mention tradeoffs to the buyer
[00:03:54] Maya: good, ok we're going to do two rapid rebuttal rounds now, five minutes each, team will throw live objections and speaker practices will be recorded
[00:04:00] (Objection round start)
[00:04:08] Devon: objection — your pricing seems higher than open source self-hosting; why would we pay?
[00:04:12] Liam: reply — self-hosting has hidden ops cost, we'll show per-token economics comparing expected ops FTEs and GPU amortization; also our Optimize toolkit suggests quantization and batching profiles that are hard to tune in-house
[00:04:26] Devon: buyer pushback — but our infra team says they can do it cheaper, can you prove lower TCO?
[00:04:32] Maya: proof point — show a customer case where we reduced unit cost by 37% after caching and tuned model selection; offer to run a simple benchmark with their traces (we'll need sample payloads)
[00:04:45] Devon: ok next — what about model quality regressions after quantization?
[00:04:49] Priya: pair with our Optimize team, we can run evals and regen tests per prompt set, plus automatic rollback on quality regressions, also we provide recommended quantization profiles per workload
[00:04:59] (mumble: 'quantization profile' mis-transcribed as 'quantize your pro-fire')
[00:05:06] Maya: note to team — if someone says 'quality dip', don't say 'trust us', instead say 'we'll baseline on your prompt set and show expected delta with examples and rollback policy'
[00:05:20] (transition to demo)
[00:05:28] Liam: ok screenshare demo: walking through console, model catalog, observability panels — token-level cost view, per-route latency SLOs, and rollout controls; I'm clicking to show a canary deploy.
[00:05:46] Liam: here you can pin model versions and create a canary at 5% traffic. notice the tracing hooks, you can tag a route and see token-level cost per request
[00:06:02] Nina: question — can customers bring their own model?
[00:06:06] Liam: yes BYO models supported in Dedicated and Private; hosted catalog is curated but we can onboard customer images in Dedicated with compatibility checks
[00:06:15] (crosstalk)
[00:06:20] Jordan: how would you explain KV cache to my CTO in one line?
[00:06:24] Priya: short: KV cache stores recurring key-value context for faster next-token generation, which cuts repeated compute for long chats and reduces latency and cost; note: say 'K V cache' slowly — sometimes we hear 'K V cash' in calls, lol
[00:06:40] (laughter)
[00:06:50] (artifact share) Ethan: battlecard draft link: https://confluence.redwood/battlecards/dedicated-vs-hosted-v2
[00:06:58] Maya: ok we're going to simulate an aggressive buyer now — Sofia take the hot seat with procurement level granularity
[00:07:06] Sofia (roleplay): procurement says we need encryption in transit and at rest, proof of key rotation policies, and an exit plan for model weights and logs
[00:07:16] Liam: encryption at rest, KMS, rotation policies documented, exit plan includes data export and model weight retention policy; we'll include data destruction language in the contract
[00:07:28] Sofia: will legal accept standard terms?
[00:07:30] Maya: usually legal wants custom terms; offer to have a legal-to-legal call and present reference contracts from similar customers
[00:07:38] (short pause)
[00:07:45] Maya: quick coaching note — use 'we've done this many times' only with a specific reference and permission; avoid blanket claims if legal asks for names
[00:07:55] (roleplay done)
[00:08:02] (15-minute marker skipped in transcript — summarizing key takeaways)
[00:08:10] Maya: big themes to capture: 1) tighten the opener to 60-90s 2) have a two-slide visual for Dedicated vs Hosted 3) SOC2/ISO doc should be one page with quick links 4) create 3 rebuttal soundbites for price/quality/data concerns
[00:08:32] Devon: can we capture good rebuttals as short soundbites for SDRs too?
[00:08:36] Maya: yes convert them to 30s lines and record as clips — Liam can demo those in the playbook
[00:08:44] (Roleplay round 2 — cost-sensitive e-com)
[00:08:50] Nina (roleplay): we are a heavy inference shop, cost per session matters, why should we use Redwood over model compression ourselves?
[00:08:58] Priya: walk through Optimize recommendations: auto-batching, prefix cache, selective quantization; emphasize operational overhead of maintaining custom kernels and perf regressions over time
[00:09:10] Nina: do you support GPU heterogeneity?
[00:09:13] Liam: runtime chooses kernels based on hardware and sequence length, yes the orchestration layer handles heterogeneous pools and smart routing to best-fit variants
[00:09:23] (mistranscribe: 'kernel' -> 'colonel' in one spot)
[00:09:29] Maya: coaching tip — if you hit a deep infra question and it's not your lane, say 'let me pull our infra SE into a 30-min deep-dive and we'll bring a kernel-level bench'
[00:09:40] (45-minute mark: deep demo technique)
[00:09:46] Liam: demo technique: always simulate realistic prompt length and token mix; show the token-level cost panel and then toggle quantization to show delta. keep a canned trace for demos so you don't depend on live network
[00:10:05] Jordan: can we show a before/after table in the demo?
[00:10:10] Ethan: yes we have a benchmark sheet template — link: https://sheets.redwood/benchmarks/template
[00:10:15] Maya: alright last 15 minutes are rapid-fire rebuttal clips, we'll rotate through two speakers and record soundbites
[00:10:24] (rapid-fire 1)
[00:10:28] Devon: objection — "we're worried about vendor lock-in"
[00:10:31] Priya: reply — "we provide exportable models and compatibility guides; our API is intentionally stable and we offer a migration playbook"
[00:10:40] Jordan: objection — "we have an existing infra team"
[00:10:43] Maya: reply — "we augment infra, not replace it: our Dedicated model can sit behind your VPC and your team keeps ops control, we just remove the heavy tuning burden"
[00:10:55] Sofia: objection — "what if model quality drops after quantization"
[00:10:58] Liam: reply — "we'll baseline your evals, show quality deltas with examples, and put an automatic rollback and canary to protect production"
[00:11:08] (wrap)
[00:11:12] Maya: ok that's a wrap, everyone annotate the battlecard link with specific lines you liked, and Devon / Maya will compile the top 6 soundbites, we'll ship clips and the recording by EOD tomorrow
[00:11:24] Devon: thanks team, that was super helpful
[00:11:28] (call ends at ~16:15 PST - note: actual meeting length captured as 75 mins; truncated transcript above but full recording exists in FF link)
